title: Revelation Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Revelation chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Revelation Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Revelation Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Revelation 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: A star falls from heaven unto the earth
Locusts come out of the smoke
The locusts are commanded not to hurt the grass
questions.correctAnswer: A star falls from heaven unto the earth
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:1 describes the event of a star falling from heaven first.

questions.question: Who was given the key of the bottomless pit?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:1 states that the star fallen from heaven was given the key of the bottomless pit.

questions.question: What came out of the bottomless pit when it was opened?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:2 describes smoke arising out of the bottomless pit as the smoke of a great furnace.

questions.question: What effect did the smoke from the bottomless pit have on the sun and air?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:2 states that the sun and the air were darkened by reason of the smoke of the pit.

questions.question: What creatures came out of the smoke upon the earth?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:3 states that locusts came out of the smoke upon the earth.

questions.question: To what were the locusts given power?
options: As the scorpions of the earth have power
To speak with a loud voice
questions.correctAnswer: As the scorpions of the earth have power
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:3 states that the locusts were given power as the scorpions of the earth have power.

questions.question: What were the locusts commanded NOT to hurt?
options: Grass of the earth, green things, and trees
Men sealed with the seal of God
questions.correctAnswer: Grass of the earth, green things, and trees
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4 commands the locusts not to hurt the grass, any green thing, or any tree.

questions.question: Who were the locusts allowed to torment?
options: Men not having the seal of God in their foreheads
questions.correctAnswer: Men not having the seal of God in their foreheads
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4 states that the locusts were to torment only those men which have not the seal of God in their foreheads.

questions.question: How long were the locusts permitted to torment men?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:5 states that the locusts were given to torment men for five months.

questions.question: What was the nature of the torment caused by the locusts?
options: Like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man
questions.correctAnswer: Like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:5 compares the torment caused by the locusts to the torment of a scorpion sting.

questions.question: What will men do in those days of torment, according to the chapter?
options: Seek death but will not find it
questions.correctAnswer: Seek death but will not find it
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:6 states that men shall seek death and not find it.

questions.question: How are the shapes of the locusts described?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:7 describes the locusts' shapes as like horses prepared unto battle.

questions.question: The locusts had crowns like gold on their heads.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:7 states that on their heads were crowns like gold.

questions.question: The locusts' faces were described as the faces of men.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:7 states that the locusts' faces were as the faces of men.

questions.question: The text says the locusts killed the men they tormented.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:5 states that the locusts were not given to kill men but to torment them.

medium.title: Revelation Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Revelation Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What do the locusts in Revelation 9:8 have that resembles women's hair?
questions.explanation: The locusts are described as having hair like that of women in Revelation 9:8.

questions.question: What does Revelation 9:4 command the locusts not to hurt?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4 states that the locusts were commanded not to hurt the grass, trees, or any green thing.

questions.question: What were the locusts given power like in Revelation 9:3?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:3 indicates that the locusts were given power as the scorpions of the earth.

questions.question: What is the duration of torment inflicted by the locusts as stated in Revelation 9:10?
questions.explanation: According to Revelation 9:10, the locusts had the power to hurt men for five months.

questions.question: What does Revelation 9:12 indicate about the woes?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:12 explicitly states that one woe is past, with two more to come.

questions.question: What does the sixth angel hear from the golden altar in Revelation 9:13?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:13 describes the voice from the golden altar instructing the sixth angel.

questions.question: What does Revelation 9:11 say about the king of the locusts?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:11 identifies the king of the locusts as Abaddon in Hebrew.

questions.question: How does Revelation 9:9 describe the sound of the locusts' wings?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:9 notes that the sound of their wings was like the sound of many horses running to battle.

questions.question: According to Revelation 9:6, what will men seek in those days?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:6 states that men will seek death and will not find it.

questions.question: What are the locusts not allowed to kill according to Revelation 9:5?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:5 indicates that they should not kill but torment those who do not have the seal of God.

questions.question: What happens when the sixth angel sounds the trumpet, according to Revelation 9:14?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:14 reveals that the sixth angel was instructed to loose the four angels bound at the Euphrates.

questions.question: In Revelation 9:7, how are the locusts described?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:7 states that the locusts were shaped like horses prepared for battle.

questions.question: The torment from the locusts is compared to what in Revelation 9:5?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:5 compares the torment to that of a scorpion when it strikes a man.

questions.question: The name Apollyon is mentioned in Revelation 9:11.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:11 states that the name of the king is Apollyon in Greek.

questions.question: The locusts are allowed to harm anything on the earth.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4 specifies that the locusts should not hurt the grass, trees, or anything green.

hard.title: Revelation Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Revelation Chapter 9.

questions.question: What were the four angels prepared for?
options: To slay a third part of men
questions.correctAnswer: To slay a third part of men
questions.explanation: The four angels were loosed for the purpose of slaying a third part of men as stated in Revelation 9:15.

questions.question: How many horsemen were part of the army mentioned in Revelation 9?
questions.explanation: The number of the army of the horsemen was specifically stated as two hundred thousand thousand in Revelation 9:16.

questions.question: What did the horses in the vision have as breastplates?
questions.explanation: The horses had breastplates of fire, jacinth, and brimstone as described in Revelation 9:17.

questions.question: What killed the third part of men in Revelation 9?
options: By the fire, smoke, and brimstone
questions.correctAnswer: By the fire, smoke, and brimstone
questions.explanation: The third part of men was killed by the fire, smoke, and brimstone, as stated in Revelation 9:18.

questions.question: What was the power of the horses' tails compared to?
questions.explanation: The tails of the horses were like unto serpents, as described in Revelation 9:19.

questions.question: What did the rest of the men not repent of?
options: Their murders, sorceries, fornication, and thefts
questions.correctAnswer: Their murders, sorceries, fornication, and thefts
questions.explanation: The rest of the men did not repent of their murders, sorceries, fornication, and thefts as stated in Revelation 9:21.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'brimstone' in Revelation 9:17 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word for 'brimstone' refers to sulfur, which is often associated with divine judgment.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Revelation 9:20-21?
questions.explanation: The verses use parallelism to emphasize the lack of repentance among the men for their sins.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of judgment seen in Revelation 9:18?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 34:9-10 speaks of divine judgment and destruction, echoing the themes found in Revelation 9:18.

questions.question: Which other passage fulfills the theme of unrepentance seen in Revelation 9:20?
questions.explanation: Revelation 16:9 also discusses the refusal to repent despite witnessing divine judgments, paralleling Revelation 9:20.

questions.question: What comes before Revelation 9:15?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:14 states that the sixth angel sounded before Revelation 9:15.

questions.question: What was the outcome of the plagues mentioned in Revelation 9:20?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:20 indicates that the rest of the men who were not killed by the plagues did not repent.

questions.question: The number of the army of horsemen is a reflection of what in biblical numerology?
questions.explanation: The vast number of the army signifies the severity of God's judgment, reflecting the biblical theme of large numbers indicating divine action.

questions.question: True or False: The locusts were commanded to harm the grass of the earth.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4 clearly states that the locusts were commanded not to hurt the grass or any green thing.

questions.question: True or False: The horsemen had heads like lions.
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:17 states that the heads of the horses were as the heads of lions.

theological.title: Revelation Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Revelation Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Revelation 9:6 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Human sin leads to a relentless judgment where death itself flees from the sinner
God's judgment is limited by human desire for death
Humans can ultimately escape divine torment by seeking death
Divine judgment spares those who desire to die
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin leads to a relentless judgment where death itself flees from the sinner
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:6 states that men will seek death and not find it, indicating the severity and relentlessness of divine judgment upon sinners.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of demonic forces is taught in Revelation 9:11?
options: Demonic forces have a hierarchical organization under a king named Abaddon or Apollyon
Demonic activity is random and without leadership
Demons operate independently and without divine permission
The king of demons is a human prince
questions.correctAnswer: Demonic forces have a hierarchical organization under a king named Abaddon or Apollyon
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:11 identifies a king over the locusts, the angel of the bottomless pit, named Abaddon or Apollyon, revealing a structured hierarchy among demonic powers.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine sovereignty is taught in Revelation 9:15?
options: God sovereignly permits the release of the four angels for a set time to execute judgment
The angels act independently without divine authorization
God is unaware of the angels’ actions
The angels’ actions are arbitrary and unplanned
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly permits the release of the four angels for a set time to execute judgment
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:15 explains that the four angels were loosed for a specific duration to slay a third part of men, indicating God’s sovereign control over judgment timelines.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Revelation 9:1 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In Revelation 9:1, the star is given the key to the bottomless pit, demonstrating God’s sovereign control over cosmic powers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Revelation 9:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:20 notes that despite judgment, the rest of men did not repent, highlighting God’s longsuffering patience with humanity.

questions.question: How does Revelation 9:13–16 connect to the theme of divine judgment in the Old Testament?
options: It parallels the plagues of Egypt as a form of God’s judgment upon the wicked
It contradicts Old Testament teachings on divine judgment
It portrays a new form of judgment unrelated to the Old Testament
It suggests human control over divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels the plagues of Egypt as a form of God’s judgment upon the wicked
questions.explanation: The unleashing of angels from the Euphrates and the massive army reflect the Old Testament’s use of plagues and judgments as God’s means to punish sin (cf. Exodus 7–12).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Revelation 9:3–4 make with the concept of the sealed in Ezekiel 9?
options: The sealing of God’s people as protected from judgment echoes Ezekiel’s marking of the faithful
It contradicts the idea of divine protection for the faithful
It teaches that all are equally judged without exception
It implies that only trees and grass are protected
questions.correctAnswer: The sealing of God’s people as protected from judgment echoes Ezekiel’s marking of the faithful
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4 commands locusts not to harm those with God’s seal, paralleling Ezekiel 9’s marking of the faithful to be spared from judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses Revelation 9:5 and Revelation 9:10 teach about the nature of divine wrath and demonically empowered torment?
options: Divine wrath can manifest through demonically empowered agents who inflict limited but intense suffering
Divine wrath is unlimited and indiscriminate destruction
Demonic torment is unrelated to divine wrath
Divine wrath spares the wicked from suffering
questions.correctAnswer: Divine wrath can manifest through demonically empowered agents who inflict limited but intense suffering
questions.explanation: Both verses describe locust-like beings empowered to torment men for five months, showing God’s wrath using demonic agents with a limited duration and specific torment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 9:18 and Revelation 9:19 teach about the power and means of divine judgment?
options: Divine judgment operates through both verbal (mouth) and physical (tail) means of destruction
Divine judgment is purely spiritual and not physical
The power of judgment is limited to natural disasters
questions.correctAnswer: Divine judgment operates through both verbal (mouth) and physical (tail) means of destruction
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states judgment by fire, smoke, and brimstone from mouths, and verse 19 adds that tails like serpents with heads hurt men, showing multifaceted divine judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 9:20 and Revelation 9:21 teach about human sinfulness and repentance in the face of divine judgment?
options: Human sinfulness is persistent and obstinate despite clear evidence of divine judgment
All humans repent when faced with judgment
Sinfulness is eradicated by judgment alone
questions.correctAnswer: Human sinfulness is persistent and obstinate despite clear evidence of divine judgment
questions.explanation: Both verses emphasize that those not killed by the plagues still did not repent of idolatry, murder, sorcery, fornication, or theft, illustrating hardened sinfulness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Revelation 9:1-6 teaches that God arbitrarily tortures people through demonic locusts. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God’s judgment is just and targeted toward unsealed sinners, demonstrating measured wrath
It shows arbitrary cruelty without divine justice
It suggests the locusts act on their own without God's permission
It teaches that all creation suffers equally without distinction
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is just and targeted toward unsealed sinners, demonstrating measured wrath
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:4-5 clarifies that only those without God’s seal are tormented, and the torment is limited to five months, showing just and measured judgment rather than arbitrariness.

questions.question: What doctrine does Revelation 9:7 teach about the symbolic nature of apocalyptic imagery relating to spiritual warfare?
options: Apocalyptic imagery uses familiar battle symbols to convey spiritual conflict realities
Imagery is purely literal and should be understood as actual horses and crowns
The passage denies any spiritual warfare context
It teaches that human armies are the main agents of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: Apocalyptic imagery uses familiar battle symbols to convey spiritual conflict realities
questions.explanation: Verse 7’s description of locusts with crowns, faces of men, and horse forms symbolizes the intensity and organized nature of spiritual warfare, common in apocalyptic literature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Revelation 9:14 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: God’s voice commanding the release of the four angels in Revelation 9:14 illustrates His omnipotent authority over angelic beings and the unfolding judgment.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Revelation 9:17–18 make with Old Testament judgments?
options: The imagery of fire, smoke, and brimstone calls back to divine judgments such as Sodom and Gomorrah
It introduces a new type of judgment unrelated to the Old Testament
It denies any connection to Old Testament imagery
It depicts human-made weapons as the source of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The imagery of fire, smoke, and brimstone calls back to divine judgments such as Sodom and Gomorrah
questions.explanation: Revelation 9:17-18’s description recalls Old Testament divine judgments characterized by fire and brimstone, underscoring the continuity of God’s wrath.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Revelation 9:2 and Revelation 9:9 teach about the symbolic representation of spiritual judgment?
options: Spiritual judgment is portrayed through vivid natural and martial imagery to signify its severity
The imagery indicates a literal smoke and horses in the natural world
Judgment is symbolic only of human warfare
The passage denies any supernatural elements
questions.correctAnswer: Spiritual judgment is portrayed through vivid natural and martial imagery to signify its severity
questions.explanation: Verse 2’s smoke darkening sun and air and verse 9’s iron breastplates and chariot sounds use natural and military images to symbolize the power and terror of divine judgment.
